notes:
Pass on the fake backend only: `python3 -m mhs.driver check ... --backend fake` exited 0 on run 3 (G1-G7 and G9 pass, G8 warn). Evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level; no controller was attached and no hardware backend was run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null).

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the family-config card names SerialDriver, but the upstream transport frames each request as STX (0x02), the address byte '0', the ASCII command and ETX (0x03), and the command words are written in the script's __main__ block (stage.py:73-75, 82-99). A line-oriented SerialDriver cannot reproduce the frame or the address byte, so this package is a direct Driver over stage:Serial with a native.py factory; the bare commands XL+ and XS go through the upstream send, which owns the framing. No wire syntax was changed. A maintainer may want an override for this card.

No catalogue class fits. The two capabilities are x-cap extensions (catalogue_requests above). cap.motion.stop.v1 was rejected because its optional deceleration input would be accepted by the binding while the upstream XS command cannot take it; the driver does not accept a value it cannot send.

The only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: the driver declares no Limit because it has no numeric input, so the conformance suite has nothing to probe for SAFE-014 and awards CL2; the gate exempts that skip and every other CL3 test passed. There is no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning; all nine Facts cite text lines of the pinned clone. The fake has no numbers; its recorded command list and empty reply are marked # placeholder.

Not covered: there is no read capability (the upstream Serial class has no getter and the clone has no position, speed or status query); X0- is not exposed because neither README.md nor stage.py states its effect; the serial port is fixed at /dev/ttyUSB0 (stage.py:25-31) and native.py passes no option; the upstream constructor blocks until the port opens (stage.py:21-42), which a hardware operator must account for.
